questions.question: Before working inside an energized industrial control cabinet, what is the safest first action?
options: Apply lockout, test for absence of voltage, and control stored energy
questions.explanation: Lockout prevents unexpected energization. Testing proves the circuit is de-energized. Stored energy such as capacitors must also be discharged or controlled.

questions.question: Which meter is best for checking insulation resistance on a motor winding?
questions.explanation: A megohmmeter applies a test voltage to insulation. It checks leakage between windings and ground. Low resistance indicates possible insulation failure.

questions.question: A drawing shows “MCC-1 feeds P-3 through VFD-2.” What should the electrician understand?
options: Motor control centre 1 feeds pump 3 through variable frequency drive 2
Main copper cable 1 feeds panel 3 through voltage fuse device 2
Meter control circuit 1 feeds plug 3 through vent fan disconnect 2
Mechanical control cabinet 1 feeds phase 3 through fuse 2
questions.explanation: MCC means motor control centre. VFD means variable frequency drive. Equipment tags must be matched to schedules and drawings.

questions.category: Task 4 - Fabricates and installs support components
questions.question: Why must cable tray supports be installed according to spacing and load requirements?
options: To prevent sagging, damage, and mechanical failure
questions.explanation: Supports carry the weight of tray and cables. Improper spacing can cause sagging or collapse. Mechanical support protects conductors and equipment.

questions.category: Task 5 - Commissions and decommissions electrical systems
questions.question: Before energizing a new motor circuit, which check is most important?
options: Correct voltage, phase rotation, grounding, and overload settings
Number of labels on the panel door
questions.explanation: Incorrect voltage or rotation can damage equipment. Grounding and overloads protect people and motors. Pre-energization checks are part of commissioning.
